metadata.title: Agricultural diversification promotes multiple ecosystem services without compromising yield

summary: Global meta-analysis of 5,188 agricultural experiments showing diversification enhances biodiversity and soil organic carbon without reducing yields.

sections.text: Synthesis of 5,188 studies demonstrates that agricultural diversification—such as intercropping, cover cropping, and agroforestry—enhances biodiversity by 24% and soil organic carbon by 6-15%, while simultaneously strengthening pest regulation and pollination services without reducing crop yields.

Homogeneous monocultures systematically diminish natural pest suppression and beneficial insect diversity, requiring escalating chemical interventions that further disrupt below-ground and above-ground trophic webs.
